title: Plastic to apparel: an analysis of sustainable purchasing intention using a machine learning ensemble
authors: Cabrera, C.A.L.; Ong, A.K.S.; Diaz, J.F.T.; Cahigas, M.M.L.; Gumasing, M.J.J.
tldr: A study of 500 Filipino respondents found that customer perceived value and perceived behavioral control are primary factors influencing intentions to purchase apparel made from recycled plastic.
problem_and_motivation: Despite proliferation of recycled fashion products, there remains a significant gap in sustainable purchasing behavior among consumers. The fashion industry is the second-highest pollutant emitter, and understanding factors driving sustainable apparel purchases is crucial for promoting environmental responsibility.
approach: Developed a Sustainability Theory of Planned Behavior (STPB) model integrating sustainability domains with TPB.
Collected 500 valid survey responses from Filipino respondents evaluating eight behavioral factors.
Applied Random Forest Classifier (RFC) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) for classification.
Used feature selection and correlation analysis for data preprocessing and validation.
Compared model performance across different hidden layer configurations and epochs.
findings: RFC achieved 92% accuracy while ANN achieved 91% accuracy at 150 epochs with 30 hidden nodes.
Customer perceived value was the strongest predictor of behavioral intention to purchase sustainable apparel.
Perceived behavioral control significantly influenced purchasing intentions.
Perceived economic concern showed mixed effects on subjective norms and attitudes.
Perceived environmental concern positively influenced attitudes toward sustainable fashion.
key_figures_tables: Table 1: Summary of related studies → identifies gaps in sustainable fashion research.
Figure 3: Theoretical framework → illustrates STPB model with eight hypothesized factors.
Table 2: Hypothesis results → shows significant relationships between STPB constructs.

definitions.definition: Sustainability Theory of Planned Behavior - an extended TPB model integrating sustainability domains.
Theory of Planned Behavior - a framework measuring behavioral characteristics through social and individual factors.
Random Forest Classifier - an ensemble machine learning algorithm for classification tasks.
Artificial Neural Network - a computational model inspired by biological neural networks.
Customer Perceived Value - a customer's holistic evaluation of a product's utility.
Perceived Behavioral Control - an individual's belief in their capability to perform a behavior.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This study extends the Theory of Planned Behavior by integrating sustainability domains to create the STPB framework for assessing sustainable purchasing behavior in the Philippine context. It demonstrates that machine learning ensemble methods can effectively predict consumer intentions in sustainable fashion, with customer perceived value emerging as the strongest predictor.
directly_justifies: RFC and ANN models achieved over 90% accuracy in predicting sustainable apparel purchase intentions.
Customer perceived value is the primary factor influencing behavioral intentions toward sustainable clothing.
Filipino consumers show willingness to pay premium prices for environmentally friendly apparel.
limits: Study limited to Filipino respondents, limiting generalizability to other cultural contexts.
Self-reported survey data may introduce response bias.
Only two ML algorithms were compared, missing potential performance of other classifiers.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematically scanned all topic domains. The paper directly addresses 1.A (Filipino demographic as respondents), 1.C (financial behavior through purchasing intentions), and 2.C (user-declared preferences via survey). Other domains were considered but rejected: 2.A (culturally specific practices not the focus), 2.B-2.D (seasonal/cyclical patterns not examined), 3.A-3.C (expense categorization not addressed), 4.A-4.B (personal finance systems not discussed), 5.A-5.C (behavioral profiles not covered), 6.A-6.B (predictive modeling for personal finance not addressed), 7.A-7.E (budgeting strategies not covered), 8.A-8.C (anomaly detection not relevant), 9.A-9.C (mobile design not discussed), 10.A-10.C (privacy not addressed), 11.A-11.B (engagement not covered), 12.A-12.C (evaluation not focused on PFMS), 13.A-13.C (savings/debt not covered), 14.A-14.C (ML deployment not addressed).

limitations: Study limited to Filipino respondents, which may limit generalizability to other populations.
Self-reported survey data may introduce social desirability bias.
The study only compared RFC and ANN, not exploring other potentially suitable classifiers.
Longitudinal data would better capture actual purchasing behavior versus intentions.
